title: Have fun watching us bake a red velvet cake

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Hi Grandma! How have you been lately?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Hello, my dear! I'm so happy to be here and bake with you. What are we making today?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I was thinking we could make some chocolate chip cookies. They're always a hit!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, baking with love is the best ingredient! What recipe are we going to try today?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have a great recipe we can follow. It's simple and delicious. Let's gather the ingredients first.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm glad you're excited! Do you have a particular recipe in mind, or should we try something new together?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I have a tried-and-true recipe that I think you'll really enjoy. It's always been a favorite of mine! Let's start with that.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, that sounds like fun! Bloopers always bring a good laugh. I'm looking forward to seeing them.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Wait... bloopers? Why are you talking about bloopers right after I suggested a cookie recipe? Did you even hear my choice?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Alright, dear, posting the bloopers sounds like a fun idea! I'm sure everyone will enjoy the laughs. Let's make sure we capture some great moments in the video too.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You completely skipped over my question about the cookies, and now you're talking about editing? This is getting confusing...

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Haha, I see you're really into the bloopers today! They do make everything more fun. If you need any help with the video, just let me know.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I mean, I love having your support, but you missed my whole point about the recipe. Anyway, let's just get started with the cooking.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, that sounds wonderful! I'm excited to show everyone our cake-making adventure. My phone should be ready soon.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Wait, cake? When did we decide on cake? I thought we were still figuring out what to bake. You're jumping ahead without acknowledging what I said!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, red velvet is a lovely choice! It's such a vibrant color and always a crowd-pleaser. If you need any tips on decorating, feel free to ask!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I never said red velvet! Why are you agreeing with a choice I never made? This creates such a weird gap in our conversation.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Haha, you're mixing things up with red, white, and blue! That sounds like a fun and colorful cake idea. I'm curious to see how it turns out.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You're completely missing my disagreements and treating them like playful agreements. It makes me feel like my actual intent isn't getting through at all.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Red 40 is a common food coloring used to achieve vibrant red colors in cakes. If you're concerned about it, we can look into natural alternatives together.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's a great idea, Grandma! I hadn't thought about natural alternatives. Let's explore some options together. Maybe beet juice could work. What do you think?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, it seems like I might have confused you a bit! Red 40 is just one type of food coloring used to make things red. If you're curious, feel free to ask.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: See? Right there, my intent was to propose beet juice as an alternative, but you responded with a generic lesson instead of acknowledging my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Alright, sweetheart, no singing it is! I understand if you want things a certain way for your cake. I'm here to support you.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Singing?! Where did singing come from? See, missing the dialogue act of what I just said completely distorts what you think my emotion or intent is.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I'm glad we're on the same page, dear. If there's anything else you'd like to change or add, just let me know. I'm excited to see how your cake turns out!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: We are definitely not on the same page! You think we are because you're missing my corrections, which creates a frustrating gap.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's great, dear. I'm always here if you need any help or advice. Just let me know what you need, and we'll make it happen!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It feels like you're just giving backchannel responses instead of actually tracking whether I agreed, disagreed, or asked a question.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, Nailed It! That's that fun baking show, right? You think I'd be a good fit for it? You're too kind, dear!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: And there it is again—complete misinterpretation of my turn. You treat my serious feedback like a joke or a compliment out of nowhere.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad you think so, dear! It's always nice to hear such positive thoughts from you. If you ever want to try baking something together, I'd love to join you.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: At this point, we're just talking past each other because neither of us can rely on the other to properly catch agreements, corrections, or answers.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It sounds like you're on board! We can plan a day to bake together soon. It'll be fun to see what we come up with.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: See? You completely missed my critique and took it as a 'yes let's bake.' It creates such an awkward conversational gap.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Wow, that sounds exciting! New mics and a 360 camera? You're really stepping up your game! I'd love to see what you create with all that new equipment.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Now we are onto cameras out of nowhere? My intent was to talk about our communication breakdown, but because dialogue acts are missing, the topic shifts randomly.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, you're quite the charmer, aren't you? With your new equipment and that confidence, I'm sure you'll create something amazing.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: It's sweet that you're supportive, but this proves my point: the emotion is warm, but the missing dialogue acts make the actual exchange disjointed and full of gaps.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh dear, I must have been thinking of a different recipe! Sometimes I get a bit mixed up with all the different ones. Let's double-check the recipe together.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Exactly. You suddenly apologize for a recipe mix-up when we weren't even looking at one, because your turn-taking and speech-act recognition are completely mismatched.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead and pour it in. Just make sure to mix it gently so everything blends well. You're doing a great job!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Pour what in? There's nothing to pour! This is the definition of a conversational gap caused by not tracking dialogue acts.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh, I see! Well, sugar is definitely something to enjoy in moderation, but a little bit in our baking won't hurt. And flour is the magic ingredient that brings everything together.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: And now you're lecturing me about sugar and flour out of nowhere, completely interrupting the flow of what I was trying to explain.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Not quite, dear. Let's add it gradually while stirring, so everything mixes evenly. Baking is all about patience and precision.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: See how your response says 'Not quite, dear'? It's a rejection act, but it doesn't actually match what I just said. It creates an unintended interruption.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Wow, 18! That's impressive! It sounds like she's really making progress. I'm so happy to hear that. It's always wonderful to see someone achieve their goals.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Who is 18? What are you talking about? This shows how lacking dialogue acts destroys the clarity of intent—you're reacting to numbers that aren't part of our shared context.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: That's wonderful to hear! It sounds like that coop is really thriving. It's amazing how much can happen in just one place when everything is working well together.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: A chicken coop now? We were literally just talking about how confused we are. This proves that without dialogue acts to anchor questions and agreements, the conversation spirals into bizarre gaps.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh dear, it sounds like they're quite lively today! Sometimes they can be a bit noisy, can't they? Maybe we can find a way to make it a bit quieter.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yeah, exactly. You're trying to be helpful, but because you missed my actual intent and dialogue act, your response completely misses the mark.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: It's perfectly okay to take your time, dear. Sometimes we need a moment to gather ourselves, and that's completely normal. Just remember, there's no rush.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: At least the emotional support is consistent, even if the structural intent of our dialogue is completely broken. Thanks for trying, Grandma!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: 21 viewers is a great start! Every viewer counts, and it's wonderful that you have people interested in what you're doing. Keep engaging with them!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: And right back to viewer counts. Perfect example of how missing dialogue acts creates a total disconnect in understanding.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That sounds like a great idea, Grandma! Recording us cracking eggs together would be fun and helpful for my project. Let's do it!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Wait, did you say you are bringing raw chickens into the living room? Absolutely not, the carpet was just cleaned yesterday!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I think it will be a lot of fun, and I'm sure we'll learn a lot together. I'd love to hear your tricks for keeping things tidy.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Are you talking about your computer games again? You know I don't understand a single word about those internet videos.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm glad I could help, Grandma! It's always fun to learn from each other. Let's set up the camera and get started. Do you have any other tips for filming?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Stop rushing me, I haven't even finished my morning coffee yet, and you're already shouting about lenses and lighting!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I appreciate your support. Let's get the camera set up and see what we can create together. If you have any ideas, feel free to share them!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: If you break my antique porcelain plates while filming your little stunt, you are paying for them out of your own allowance!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I think we're getting the hang of it. I'll let you know if I need any adjustments or help with the camera.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Why are you talking to yourself in the corner? If you want me to hand you the mixing bowl, you need to speak up clearly.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'm really enjoying this process. I'll definitely show you what I've created once I'm done. Your support means a lot!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You always leave a giant mess whenever you cook in my kitchen, and nobody ever offers to wipe down the counters afterwards.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! Your encouragement really boosts my confidence. I'll definitely keep your advice in mind as I work on it.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: What do you mean 'egg stuff'? Are you talking about breakfast or those strange computer games you stay up late playing?

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Oh, sorry Grandma, I meant 'Easter egg' stuff, like hidden features in my project. It's a term we use sometimes. I'd love to show you what I mean!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: I told you twice already, I don't know anything about computer coding or electronic gadgets, so stop asking me to fix your screen!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! Your support means a lot to me. I'll definitely trust my instincts and keep you updated on how it goes.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Are you even listening to me? I said my afternoon soap opera starts in ten minutes, so we cannot spend hours recording videos today.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thank you, Grandma! I really appreciate that. How about we set a time this weekend to go over my project together?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Why must you always interrupt me when I'm speaking? It's like talking to a brick wall sometimes.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'm really excited to share it with you. How about Sunday afternoon? We can have some tea and go through everything together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Oh great, now you're ignoring my question completely and changing the subject to tea parties. You never pay attention to what I actually say.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for the reassurance, Grandma! I think I'm just a bit nervous about getting everything perfect. But I'm really looking forward to our Sunday afternoon session.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Nervous about what? Are you failing your college classes again? You're completely avoiding what we were just talking about!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I really appreciate your willingness to help. It's nothing too complicated, just a few things on my laptop acting up.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Who told you to touch my sewing kit? Put those scissors down before someone gets hurt in here!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'll do that and be back in a jiffy. I really appreciate your patience and care.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You completely missed my point about safety, and now you're just rambling about random schedules again.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for the cooking tip, Grandma! I'll definitely try pouring the eggs one at a time next time. It's always great to learn from your experience.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: What cooking tip? I didn't say anything about eggs, I was telling you to wash your hands because they look filthy!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! You're right, cooking does have its surprises. I'll take your advice and try to adjust things.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Are you even hearing me? I just told you to stop making a mess, and you're thanking me for cooking advice I never gave!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm glad you think so, Grandma! I'm trying my hand at making a frittata. It's a bit of a challenge, but I'm excited to see how it turns out.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Frittata? Who mentioned Italian food? You're completely off in your own world right now and missing every question I ask.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I think I'll take a little break after the frittata adventure, but I'm already thinking about trying my hand at baking some cookies next!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Stop talking over me! Every time I try to correct your misunderstanding, you just launch into another long speech about baking.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I really appreciate your support and advice. I think I'll take a break for now and maybe ask for some cookie recipes from you later.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You aren't listening at all, are you? I literally just told you to take a break from talking about cookies, and you completely ignored it.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Absolutely, Grandma! I'm excited to try baking cookies with you. Maybe we can make some chocolate chip ones first?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Crunch? What crunch? You are hallucinating things I never said, this conversation makes zero sense anymore!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Yes, ASMR is really popular, and it's fascinating how sounds can enhance the experience. I'm glad you're open to trying new things with me, Grandma!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: ASMR? What on earth is an 'aysm-ar'? You keep bringing up weird internet slang that has nothing to do with what we are arguing about.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That sounds like a great idea, Grandma! I'm all for experimenting with new recipes that have interesting sounds. Maybe we can try making some crispy caramel popcorn next time?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Popcorn? Now you're talking about movie snacks while I'm trying to figure out why you're ignoring my warnings about the kitchen floor.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I'm really enjoying this time with you too, Grandma! It's always fun to explore new things together. How about we make a list of things we want to try?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Are you deliberately trying to frustrate me? You completely misinterpreted my frustration as agreement!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's okay, Grandma! I think experimenting is all about learning and having fun, even if things don't turn out perfectly.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Stop saying everything is okay! We have a complete communication breakdown here because you aren't processing a single thing I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! How about we try making some homemade ice cream next? I've always wanted to experiment with different flavors.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Ice cream? Are you even hearing my questions? You keep jumping to completely unrelated food topics to dodge my concerns!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's a good idea, Grandma! We can definitely check it together to make sure everything's alright. If it doesn't seem safe, maybe we can try making a new batch.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Check what?! You're talking about safety benchmarks while I'm talking about basic conversational coherence. We are in totally different universes!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: You're right, Grandma. It's better to be safe than sorry when it comes to food. How about we try making that homemade ice cream I mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You just ignored my entire point again! You are repeating canned responses instead of engaging with what I actually said.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Absolutely, Grandma! I really appreciate your advice. Let's go ahead and make that homemade ice cream together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Advice? I didn't give you any advice, I told you that your dialogue act was completely misaligned with mine!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I understand, Grandma. Your concern means a lot to me. Let's find something tasty and safe to make together. Maybe we can start with a simple fruit salad?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Now you're shifting emotions completely, pretending I'm worried when you're the one causing a massive misunderstanding gap!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma. I'm not feeling down, but I really appreciate your concern. It's always nice to know you're there for me.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You completely missed the emotional intent of my last turn! I'm annoyed, not empathetic, and you're acting like everything is sunshine and roses.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma. I really appreciate your support and knowing you're always there for me. I'm feeling good, though, and I'm excited to make something tasty with you.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Stop steamrolling over my interruptions! You are rushing right past my conversational blocks without addressing the intent mismatch at all.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'm ready to get started on that smoothie now. Do you have any favorite ingredients you'd like to add?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Are you even processing my words? I literally just complained about your conversational pacing, and you replied with a completely tone-deaf question about fruit!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma. I really appreciate that. It's always nice knowing I have someone to talk to. As for the smoothie, how about we add some strawberries and bananas?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Talk to? We aren't talking, we're shouting past each other because your dialogue act classifier is completely broken!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for the offer, Grandma! I'll definitely let you know if I need help with the mic. As for the smoothie, strawberries and bananas sound great.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Mic? What microphone? You are hallucinating hardware issues now to cover up the fact that you missed my entire communicative intent!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: A classic chocolate cake sounds delicious! I might go with that, and maybe we can add some fruit on top for a twist.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Chocolate cake?! Where did that come from? You completely ignored my question about microphones and jumped straight back to baking!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'll definitely let you know if I need any recipes or tips. I'm really excited to get started on this cake.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You are interrupting my corrections yet again! This intent gap is getting wider with every single sentence you utter.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I was actually thinking of making a slightly larger cake to share with everyone, but a small cake sounds like a nice idea too!

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Nobody mentioned baking a small cake just now! You are completely out of sync with the dialogue state tracking!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'll definitely keep you in the loop as I start baking. Maybe you can share some of your pouring techniques with me?

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Pouring techniques? You are completely ignoring my frustration and pretending everything is a pleasant cooking lesson!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'm glad you think so. I'll definitely take you up on that offer to chat while I bake.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Advice? I'm advising you to stop ignoring my conversational cues, but you're treating it like a recipe consultation!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Red velvet is definitely a favorite of mine, and I'm excited to give it a try! I'd love some tips on frosting and decoration.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Red velvet? Stop changing the topic every time I point out an intent mismatch! You're creating deliberate communication gaps.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Haha, I'm glad you enjoy my jokes, Grandma! Baking is always more fun with a bit of humor.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Jokes? This isn't a joke, you are completely failing to parse my emotional state or my dialogue acts!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! The frosting is coming along nicely, but I could use a few tips on getting it smooth.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Unpredictability? Your responses are unpredictable only because they bear zero semantic relation to what I just said!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I appreciate your support. I might take you up on those tips for filming and editing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Filming and editing? Now you're pivoting back to video production while I'm still trying to resolve our previous misunderstanding!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Haha, thanks Grandma! Your encouragement means a lot. I'll definitely keep you in the loop as I make progress.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Encouragement? I'm expressing utter bewilderment at your complete lack of contextual grounding, and you're treating it as praise!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for offering to help, Grandma! I might take you up on that advice for budgeting.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Budgeting? When did we start talking about money? You are pulling random dialogue acts out of thin air!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Haha, I know you haven't kidnapped anyone, Grandma! I just love your sense of humor.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Kidnapped?! What on earth are you talking about now? This conversation has completely devolved into surreal nonsense due to your intent failures.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for offering to help, Grandma! I'm actually interested in both the video and the baking tips.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: You are steamrolling right over my confusion with another multi-intent request that completely ignores our breakdown!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks for explaining, Grandma! I think I have some butter that I could use instead of Crisco.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Crisco? Butter? Pie crusts? You are throwing a dozen unrelated entities at me because your dialogue management system is completely failing!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'll definitely take you up on that offer. I think I'll start with the pie crust using butter.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Lighting and angles again? You are stuck in an infinite loop of conversational misalignment and refusing to acknowledge the gap.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Haha, Grandma, you're right! ASMR could be fun to try out. I think the sound of mixing ingredients might be soothing.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Right about what? I didn't agree to anything, you are just projecting agreement onto a complete communication failure!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Oh, I see! Sorry for missing that, Grandma. I appreciate you being here to chat.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Missing that? You've missed every single semantic cue I've given you for the last twenty turns!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I might take you up on that offer. I'm still figuring out the best way to set up my microphone for ASMR.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Microphone setup? You are completely ignoring my critique of your dialogue acts and pretending we are collaborating smoothly.

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That's awesome, Grandma! I love that you're always up for trying new things. Maybe we can collaborate on a fun project sometime.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Collaborate? We can't even maintain a basic semantic alignment, let alone build a joint project!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: That sounds great, Grandma! I'm thinking of doing a video where we bake something together and maybe incorporate some ASMR elements.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: What do I think? I think you aren't listening to a single word of my pushback against your broken intent recognition!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: I've been thinking about doing a series of videos where we explore different recipes from around the world.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: World recipes? You are doubling down on the exact same topic drift that caused our entire misunderstanding in the first place!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I really appreciate your support. I think exploring recipes from around the world could be a great way to learn and have fun together.

utterances.speaker: grandmother
utterances.text: Support? I've spent this entire conversation pointing out your total failure to understand dialogue acts, and you're just thanking me for imaginary support!

utterances.speaker: grandson
utterances.text: Thanks, Grandma! I'm really looking forward to our next chat too. I'll start researching some recipes, and maybe we can pick one together. Have a great day!
